rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect depicts belief as continually renewed and passed from elders to younger generations, which its adherents do not abandon.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالمضارع في { يظنون } لأنهم يحددون هذا الظن ويتلقاه صغيرهم عن كبيرهم في أجيالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They settled on denying resurrection through superstitions and fanciful analogies; when Quranic proofs came, they answered with obstinate demands to bring back their ancestors.
rows.anchor: عقدوا على عقيدة أن لا حياة بعد الممات استنادا للأوهام والأقيسة الخيالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses are Quranic proofs of resurrection, as the surrounding discourse makes clear; their demand exposes flight from argument into helpless obstinacy.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالآيات آيات القرآن المتعلقة بالبعث بدليل ما قبل الكلام وما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “bring our fathers” addresses believers, including the Messenger; calling this utterance their proof records their evasive move from clear evidence.
rows.anchor: والخطاب بفعل { ائتوا } موجه للمؤمنين بدخول الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes “proof” ironically: the connected exception mocks them by calling killing “hospitality,” as in ʿAmr b. Kulthum’s verse.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التهكم بهم كقول عمرو بن كلثوم : قريناكم فعجلنا قراكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “proof” is a connected exception using their own imagined standard, a figurative image of what they mistakenly regard as evidence.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يكون إطلاق اسم الحجة على كلامهم جرى على اعتقادهم وتقديرهم دون قصد تهكم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading uses “proof” by contrariety, ironically meaning they have no proof at all; the poet Jarran al-ʿAwdi illustrates this rhetorical denial.
rows.anchor: استعارة بعلاقة الضدية فيكون مجازا مرسلا بتنزيل التضاد منزلة التناسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulu al-ʿazm means people marked by resolve: a firmly formed intention to act or speak without hesitation; the author cites Quranic usage and Saʿd b. Nashib’s verse.
rows.anchor: وأولوا العزم : أصحاب العزم ، أي المتصفون به . والعزم : نية محققة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religiously praiseworthy resolve seeks purification of the self and welfare of the community; it rests on patience through hardship, piety, and vigilant self-accounting.
rows.anchor: والعزم المحمود في الدين : العزم على ما فيه تزكية النفس وصلاح الأمة ، وقوامه الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s lack of resolve occurred before his descent into the realm of moral obligation.
rows.anchor: وهذا قبل هبوط آدم إلى عالم التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the author’s reading, min in “among the messengers” is partitive, meaning only some messengers were Ulu al-ʿazm.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا تكون { من } في قوله : { من الرسل } تبعيضية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says all messengers are Ulu al-ʿazm; on this view min is explanatory.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال : كل الرسل أولو عزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes Muhammad among Ulu al-ʿazm: the commanded comparison makes his obedient patience like theirs, and whoever bears their patience belongs among them.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية اقتضت أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم من أولي العزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns hastening punishment for the polytheists; delay does not conflict with resolve and lengthens the Messenger’s patience, strengthening his resolve.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستعجال ينافي العزم ولأن في تأخير العذاب تطويلا لمدة صبر الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of “hasten” is punishment or destruction; the lām means “for their sake,” with an omitted noun meaning hastening their destruction.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { تستعجل } محذوف دل عليه المقام ، تقديره : العذاب أو الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their seeing the promised punishment as if after only an hour explains the ban: its arrival is certain, so delay or haste does not change its occurrence.
rows.anchor: تعليل للنهي عن الاستعجال لهم بالعذاب بأن العذاب واقع بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet Murra b. ʿAdāʾ al-Faqʿasī may have drawn his image of a night seeming absent once a goal is reached from this verse.
rows.anchor: قال مرة بن عداء الفقعسي ، ولعله أخذ قوله من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Of a day” describes the hour: daytime seems short because people are occupied, while a sleepless night drags; the indefinite hour conveys a small span.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصها بهذا الوصف لأن ساعة النهار تبدو للناس قصيرة لما للناس في النهار من الشواغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this minimization to the Friday hour for answered prayer, which the Prophet indicated with a gesture showing its shortness.
rows.anchor: كما في حديث الجمعة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( وفيه ساعة يستجاب فيها الدعاء ) ، وأشار بيده يقللها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A communication” summarizes what preceded for believers and unbelievers; it is the predicate of an omitted “this,” as in titles and document headings.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { بلاغ } خبر مبتدإ محذوف تقديره : هذا بلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative may be stated explicitly, as in “this is a communication for people” and “in this is a message for worshippers.”
rows.anchor: وقد يظهر اسم الإشارة كما في قوله تعالى : { هذا بلاغ للناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summary is a fresh introductory conclusion, comparable to the Quranic phrases “those are ten complete” and “that was a community that passed away.”
rows.anchor: مثل جملة { تلك عشرة كاملة } ( البقرة : 196 ) ، { تلك أمة قد خلت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final question functions as a negation, allowing an exception: only the wicked are destroyed, as in the question about turning from Abraham’s religion.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في النفي ، ولذلك صح الاستثناء منه كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion follows from earlier statements about the Messenger, the warning to wrongdoers, and the destruction of surrounding towns: only wicked polytheists perish.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يهلك إلا القوم الفاسقون ، وذلك من قوله : { قل ما كنت بدعا من الرسل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction is literal in accounts such as ʿĀd and figurative for the wretched condition of afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: فإن ما حكي فيما مضى بعضه إهلاك حقيقي مثل ما في قصة عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definite “the people” can mean the whole class of wicked people, universalizing the warning, or the known polytheists just mentioned; the latter substitution hints that shirk causes destruction.
rows.anchor: أي القوم المتحدث عنهم في قوله : { كأنهم يوم يرون ما يوعدون } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect can combine future destruction of Meccan polytheists with the destruction of earlier nations; here wickedness means abandoning faith through shirk.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالفسق هنا الفسق عن الإيمان وهو فسق الإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception indicates that others escape this destruction: those who believed and acted righteously.
rows.anchor: أو هم الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is most commonly called Muhammad in hadith collections and tafsirs, after the Prophet’s name in its second verse, earlier than the occurrence in Ali ʿImran.
rows.anchor: سميت هذه السورة في كتب السنة سورة محمد . وكذلك ترجمت في ( صحيح البخاري )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also called al-Qital because it treats the legislation of fighting; the author considers the phrase “a surah in which fighting is mentioned” a Quranic basis for the title.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميتها سورة القتال فلأنها ذكرت فيها مشروعية القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari call it “Surah Those Who Disbelieved,” while the author says Muhammad is the more famous title.
rows.anchor: ووقع في أكثر روايات ( صحيح البخاري ) سورة الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage responds to some Meccan Jews who said God created the heavens and earth in six days and rested on the seventh, as Genesis states; rest implies fatigue.
rows.anchor: والاستراحة تؤذن بالنصب والإعياء فلما فرغت الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the verses refuted polytheists, the discourse turns to refute Jews who spoke of divine rest; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports consensus that the whole surah is Meccan, so a Medina-only setting is strained.
rows.anchor: مع ما حكى ابن عطية من الإجماع على أن هذه السورة كلها مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six-day creation statement completes the earlier account of the heavens and leads to “no weariness touched Us,” refuting the Jewish claim.
rows.anchor: تكملة لما وصف من خلق السماوات في قوله : { أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation statement is coordinated as a new narrative and interrupts the previous speech before the conclusion drawn from it.
rows.anchor: والجملة معطوفة على الجملة التي قبلها عطف القصة على القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in “and no weariness touched Us” is circumstantial, emphasizing that this immense creation in a short period did not tire its Creator.
rows.anchor: والواو في { وما مسنا من لغوب } واو الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah stresses divine power to establish resurrection against polytheists’ doubts; “touch” denies even the weakest degree of fatigue, as in the marital expression “before they touch.”
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الآيات كلها مشتملة على إبراز معنى سعة القدرة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lughub means exhaustion caused by running or strenuous work.
rows.anchor: واللغوب : الإعياء من الجري والعمل الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be patient follows the preceding discourse and consoles the Prophet amid denial of resurrection and his message; “what they say” gathers both charges.
rows.anchor: أي فاصبر على ما يقول المشركون من التكذيب بما أخبرتهم من البعث وبالرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they say” refers to the polytheists addressed by the admonitions beginning with their surprise at a warner from among themselves.
rows.anchor: وضمير { يقولون } عائد إلى المشركين الذين هم المقصود من هذه المواعظ والنذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts that ʿUqba b. Abi Muʿayṭ put camel entrails on the Prophet while he prostrated; Abu Bakr pulled him away and invoked the case of a man who says “My Lord is God.”
rows.anchor: مثل قصة إلقاء عقبة بن أبي معيط سلا الجزور على ظهر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also connects the mockery of worshippers to the Quranic rebuke of one who forbids a servant from praying.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih here means prayer, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya says exegetes unanimously held; the verb becomes intransitive like “pray,” and “with praise” fits recitation of al-Fatiha in each unit.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : أجمع المتأولون على أن التسبيح هنا الصلاة

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet likens seeing God to seeing the moon and urges preserving prayer before sunrise and sunset, identified as dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله : ( كنا جلوسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ نظر إلى القمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the prayer before sunset as noon and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : قبل الغروب : الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the prayer before sunset as the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : العصر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand night-time tasbih as prayer; Abu al-Aḥwaṣ instead takes it as saying “Glory be to God.”
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أن التسبيح فيه هو الصلاة ، وعن أبي الأحوص

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the night prayers as Maghrib and ʿIsha.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : صلاة المغرب وصلاة العشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The span before sunset begins when the sun passes its zenith and ends at sunset, covering noon and afternoon prayer; night prayer means Maghrib and ʿIsha, since the night began at sunset in their calendar.
rows.anchor: يبتدىء من زوال الشمس عن كبد السماء لأنها حين تزول عن كبد السماء قد مالت إلى الغروب

rows.speaker: أبو برزة
rows.claim: An alternative takes all the times as supererogatory prayers: two units before sunrise and two before sunset.
rows.anchor: والذي قبل الغروب ركعتان قبل غروب الشمس قاله أبو برزة وأنس بن مالك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: On the supererogatory-prayer interpretation, Mujahid identifies the night prayer as night vigil.
rows.anchor: والذي من الليل قيام الليل قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alternative raises whether the command recommends prayers generally or imposes them specifically on the Prophet; the author points ahead to Surat al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: ويأتي على هذا الوجه الاختلاف في محمل الأمر على الندب إن كانا عاما أو على الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the prayer schedule to the commands in al-Insan and al-Tur.
rows.anchor: وقريب من هذه الآية قوله تعالى : { فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تطع منهم آثما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After the prostrations” may coordinate either with “before sunrise” or with “glorify Him at night.”
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون معطوفا على قوله : { قبل طلوع الشمس } ، ويجوز أن يكون معطوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idbar literally means turning away and is metaphorical for completion; prostration means prayer, and the phrase functions as a time adverb meaning after prayer ends.
rows.anchor: والإدبار : بكسر الهمزة حقيقته : الانصراف لأن المنصرف يستدبر من كان معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu Jaʿfar, Hamza, and Khalaf read idbār with a kasra; the others read adbar with a fatḥa as the plural of dabr, “end.” Both indicate the end of prayer.
rows.anchor: وقرأه نافع وابن كثير وأبو جعفر وحمزة وخلف بكسر همزة { إدبار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No, I swear” can mean “I swear,” with extra la emphasizing caution against a false oath; alternatively it signals that the truth is so evident no oath is needed, a usage that became emphatic assertion.
rows.anchor: و { لا أقسم } بمعنى : أقسم ، و ( لا ) مزيدة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the no-need-for-an-oath sense as better matching Quranic parallels; either reading draws attention to the worthiness of the sworn subject.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه الثاني هو الأنسب بما وقع من مثله في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading, “it is a great oath” means the mentioned object is something great that people swear by; “oath” is a verbal noun used for its object.
rows.anchor: فإطلاق قسم عليه من إطلاق المصدر وإرادة المفعول

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr and some exegetes treat la as an independent reply to denials that the Quran is poetry, magic, ancient tales, or a soothsayer’s speech; “I swear” then begins a new statement.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير وبعض المفسرين : أنهم جعلوا ( لا ) حرفا مستقلا عن فعل { أقسم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the oath follows the signs that establish resurrection and refutes the opponents’ claims about the Quran.
rows.anchor: وعليه بمعنى الكلام مع فاء التفريع أنه تفرع على ما سطع من أدلة إمكان البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawaqiʿ can mean places where fixed and wandering stars fall or set; their ordered motions and alternation display a wondrous system and the Creator’s greatness.
rows.anchor: و { مواقع النجوم } جمع موقع يجوز أن يكون مكان الوقوع ، أي محال وقوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wuquʿ can also mean settling in a place, so star sites may be their locations and courses, like the sky’s constellations.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الوقوع على الحلول في المكان ، يقال : وقعت الإبل ، إذا بركت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sites are the stars’ precisely regulated orbits, constellations, and lunar mansions.
rows.anchor: والمواقع هي : أفلاك النجوم المضبوطة السير في أفق السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either interpretation honors the stars because their courses reveal divine wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: وذكر ( مواقع النجوم ) على كلا المعنيين تنويه بها وتعظيم لأمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawaqiʿ may be the plural of the mimetic verbal noun for occurrence.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( مواقع ) جمع موقع المصدر الميمي للوقوع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة
rows.claim: Some exegetes read najm as a portion or installment and take the “stars” as successive portions of Quranic revelation, making the oath directly about the Quran.
rows.anchor: وهو عن ابن عباس وعكرمة فيؤول إلى القسم بالقرآن على حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It is a great oath, if you knew” is parenthetical between the oath and its answer; the pronoun may refer to the oath, its object, or the sworn matter.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم } معترضة بين القسم وجوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you knew” is nested parenthesis between a described noun and its adjective.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لو تعلمون } معترضة بين الموصوف وصفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to the oath, the missing knowledge is detailed understanding of star sites: their signs should lead to monotheism, but the polytheists failed to infer it.
rows.anchor: ودليل انتفاء علمهم بعظمته أنهم لم يدركوا دلالة ذلك على توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to the sworn matter, the sense is that full knowledge of it would make an oath unnecessary.
rows.anchor: فأما إن جعلت ضمير { وإنه لقسم } عائدا إلى المقسم عليه فالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read mawāqiʿ in the plural; Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read singular mawqiʿ, a mimetic noun for setting or its place.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { بمواقع } بصيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular reading can mean the stars’ setting, comparable to the Lord of east and west.
rows.anchor: أي بوقوعها ، أي غروبها ، أو هو اسم لجهة غروبها كقوله : { رب المشرق والمغرب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “you know” is omitted and supplied as the greatness or evidence of greatness; alternatively, the verb is intransitive: “if you had knowledge.”
rows.anchor: ومفعول { تعلمون } محذوف دل عليه الكلام ، أي لو تعلمون عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “it is a noble Quran” has no expressed antecedent because the Quran is already mentally present to the audience.
rows.anchor: وضمير { إنه لقرآن كريم } راجع إلى غير مذكور في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran literally means recited speech, repeatedly read and contemplated; the author links this usage to another Quranic occurrence.
rows.anchor: والقرآن : الكلام المقروء ، أي المتلو المكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karim means precious and exalted; the Quran surpasses earlier divine books through comprehensive guidance, evidence, refutation, clarity, concision, eloquence, and sound.
rows.anchor: والكريم : النفيس الرفيع في نوعه كما تقدم عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In a hidden book” is an honorific metaphor, not literal description; the preposition “in” marks figurative containment.
rows.anchor: فليس لفظ { كتاب } ولا وصف { مكنون } مرادا بهما الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers in all God’s messengers are the true ṣiddiqun; this contrasts with Jews who reject Jesus and Muhammad and Christians who reject Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والمؤمنون آمنوا برسل الله كلهم ، ولذلك وصفوا بأنهم الصديقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddiq is an intensive form of “one who confirms,” usually from a triliteral root but sometimes from an augmented form; the author illustrates flexible derivation with Arabic usage and poetry.
rows.anchor: والصديق بتشديد الدال مبالغة في المصدق مثل المسيك للشحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deserve the title because they affirmed every true messenger without partisanship; the separating pronoun restricts true ṣiddiqun to them, excluding People of the Book who rejected some messengers.
rows.anchor: لأنهم صدقوا جميع الرسل الحق ولم تمنعهم عن ذلك عصبية ولا عناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative honors the believers and signals that the qualities just named make them worthy of what follows.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة للتنويه بشأنهم وللتنبيه على أن المشار إليهم استحقوا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Mujahid, Zayd b. Aslam, and others take “the witnesses” as a second predicate of the believers: they testify about nations at judgment.
rows.anchor: وحكي هذا التأويل عن ابن مسعود ومجاهد وزيد بن أسلم وجماعة

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: A report traced from al-Baraʾ b. ʿAzib to the Prophet mentions martyrs killed in God’s path in connection with the interpretation of “witnesses.”
rows.anchor: كقتلاهم في سبيل الله وروي عن البراء بن عازب يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve in God and deny the Quran include polytheists, Jews, and Christians, though their degrees of deserved Hell differ by the particular disbelief each committed.
rows.anchor: ما يشمل المشركين واليهود والنصارى على تفاوت بينهم في دركات الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative marks them as deserving Hell because of disbelief and denial; “companions of Hell” conveys their close, lasting attachment to it.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عنهم بأصحاب مضاف إلى الجحيم دلالة على شدة ملازمتهم للجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After urging charity, the verse counters miserliness driven by preserving wealth for worldly pleasures: worldly life passes away, while life should secure lasting afterlife bliss and protection from punishment.
rows.anchor: أشير إلى أنها ينبغي أن تتخذ الحياة وسيلة للنعيم الدائم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Know” opens the exhortation in the same way as the earlier command concerning God reviving the earth.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح هذا بقوله تعالى : { اعلموا } للوجه الذي بيناه آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An open hamza in annama still conveys restriction; the six descriptions characterize the dominant concerns of most people, not every possible human act.
rows.anchor: وحصر الحياة الدنيا في الأخبار الجارية عليها هو قصر أحوال الناس في الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generalization leaves out those God preserves, whose lives serve Him through piety, benefit, kindness, support of truth, teaching virtue, and just law.
rows.anchor: إلا الذين عصمهم الله تعالى فجعل أعمالهم في الحياة كلها لوجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment is especially common in youth as people respond to aging; women may seek beauty among both women and men, not merely to attract men.
rows.anchor: ويكثر التزين في طور الفتوة لأن الرجل يشعر بابتداء زوال محاسن شبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment pervades worldly life, including homes and clothing, and can be physical or moral, the latter resembling the juristic category of embellishing interests.
rows.anchor: ويغلب التزين على أحوال الحياة فإن معظم المساكن والملابس يراد منه الزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride is self-praising speech; its reciprocal form suits boasting between people, and people boast of truly good qualities or falsely praised customs and deeds.
rows.anchor: وصيغ منه زنة التفاعل لأن شأن الفخر أن يقع بين جانبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False boasting can celebrate extravagance in wine, gambling, fornication, murder, or unjust raiding; boasting is most common in mature adulthood and can breed envy.
rows.anchor: مثل التفاخر بالإغلاء في ثمن الخمور وفي الميسر والزنى والفخر بقتل النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takathur is an intensive reciprocal form: people compete to possess more of what they value; the usage later broadened to seeking abundance without direct rivalry.
rows.anchor: فكان المرء ينظر في الكثرة من الأمر المحبوب إلى امرىء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi in “in wealth and children” can mean because of them or figuratively treat them as a setting in which people accumulate more.
rows.anchor: إما مستعملة في التعليل ، وإما هي الظرفية المجازية ، فإن جعلت الأموال كالظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life was designed as a means for souls to rise toward their angelic potential, as in the creation of a vicegerent on earth; people diverted that design from guidance toward eternal life.
rows.anchor: أن تكون الحياة وسيلة لبلوغ النفوس إلى ما هيأها الله له من العروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper outcome is a good life and reward for faithful righteous action, as the author links to the verse promising the best reward.
rows.anchor: فلنحيينه حياة طيبة ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile can be a new sentence with an omitted subject, “it is like rain,” or a circumstantial phrase where kamathal means “like the state of.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون في موضع خبر من مبتدأ محذوف ، أي هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The composite image compares people’s attractive, varied worldly states and their rapid passing to vegetation that rain makes flourish before it yellows and breaks apart.
rows.anchor: فشبهت هيئة أهل الدنيا في أحوالهم الغالبة عليهم والمشار إلى تنويعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vegetation is the central comparison; rain is included to portray the stages from their beginning and lend the scene beauty, as in Kaʿb b. Zuhayr’s description of water mixed with wine.
rows.anchor: والمقصود بالتمثيل هو النبات ، وإنما ابتدىء بغيث تصويرا للهيئة من مبادئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes commonly gloss yahīj as drying, but the author notes they supplied no Arabic poetic evidence; al-Raghib and al-Asas describe yellowing or beginning to dry.
rows.anchor: تضافرت كلمات المفسرين على تفسير يهيج ب ( ييبس ) أو يجف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers “thickens and approaches dryness”: the root suggests agitation, and thickening crops rustle as they move, marking the onset of drying; al-Nabigha’s verse illustrates the root’s sense of stirring.
rows.anchor: فالوجه أن الهياج : الغلظ ومقاربة اليبس ، لأن مادة الهياج تدل على الاضطراب والثوران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks rank in the sequence because yellowing most clearly signals impending disappearance; fa marks the near-immediate yellowing that accompanies drying.
rows.anchor: وعطفت جملة يهيج } ب ( ثم ) لإفادة التراخي الرتبي لأن اصفرار النبات أعظم دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuṭām means broken fragments; the crop’s stages portray worldly youth, maturity, old age, decline, and eventual extinction.
rows.anchor: والحطام : بضم الحاء ما حطم ، أي كسر قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The composite simile also permits matching individual stages: life’s arrival, full maturity, early decline, and loss of strength and wealth correspond to the crop’s growth, thickening, yellowing, and shattering.
rows.anchor: فيشبه أول أطوار الحياة وإقبالها بالنبات عقب المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actions done for God belong to the afterlife in meaning and only appear to fall under this worldly simile; good works and learning do not decay while pursued, and some grow over time.
rows.anchor: فأعمال البر ودراسة العلم ونحو ذلك لا يعتريها نقص ما دام صاحبها مقبلا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with the afterlife warns and encourages; forgiveness and divine approval name spiritual bliss, which entails bodily pleasure suited to embodied human beings.
rows.anchor: وكني عن النعيم بمغفرة من الله ورضوان لأن النعيم قسمان مادي وروحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine approval grants the fullest delight, while forgiveness removes what could impede it; bodily pleasures are ultimately perceived by the spirit.
rows.anchor: وكان رضوان الله يقتضي إعطائهم منتهى ما به التذاذهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Worldly life is only deceptive enjoyment” contrasts the two outcomes; the omitted noun is worldly conditions, and the restriction describes the usual experience of those who seek them.
rows.anchor: والكلام على تقدير مضاف ، أي وما أحوال الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghūrūr is deception: presenting something harmful, which a sensible person would avoid, as beneficial and desirable; the genitive expresses the eventual consequence of being deceived.
rows.anchor: والغرور : الخديعة ، أي إظهار الأمر الضار الذي من شأنه أن يحترز العاقل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This conclusion recaps the passage from 57:12 and urges gaining afterlife bliss while warning against worldly adornment; it foregrounds the desired encouragement.
rows.anchor: فذلكة لما تقدم من قوله تعالى : { يوم ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات يسعى نورهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Race” expresses utmost care and rivalry in virtue, urging believers to leave behind those who settle for worldly enjoyment.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن العناية والاهتمام بفعل السابقة لإلهاب النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “forgiveness” magnifies it and lets the sentence stand independently; racing toward forgiveness means pursuing its causes.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { مغفرة } لقصد تعظيمها ولتكون الجملة مستقلة بنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿArḍ means width, not the opposite of length; the author illustrates this usage with another Quranic expression and a verse by al-ʿAdil.
rows.anchor: مستعمل في السعة وليس مقابل الطور لظهور أنه لا طائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden’s width is compared with the combined breadth of heaven and earth to evoke the greatest expanse people can imagine, not to measure it or locate it in the sky.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد تحديد ذلك العرض ولا أن الجنة في السماء حتى يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command covers every good deed leading to forgiveness and the garden, using “race” literally and figuratively; the author cites the report that people would race or draw lots for the first row.
rows.anchor: وهذا الأمر شامل لجميع المسابقات إلى أفعال البر الموجبة للمغفرة ونعيم الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is the reward of wrongdoers” concludes that the bad end of the unbeliever and his tempter also awaits those who imitate them in wronging people of guidance.
rows.anchor: والعاقبة السوأى جزاء جميع الظالمين المعتدين على الله والمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling the bloodless victory over Banu al-Naḍir, the failed hopes of their hypocrite allies, and the fate of earlier towns, the surah commands piety as gratitude for God’s favors and promises.
rows.anchor: انتقال من الامتنان على المسلمين بما يسر الله من فتح قرية بني النضير بدون قتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because worldly favors have just been recalled, believers are told to prepare for the afterlife by reflecting on what each self has sent ahead.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ما تضمنته السورة من تأييد الله إياهم وفيض نعمه عليهم كان من منافع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Let every soul consider” coordinates one command with another and interrupts the two commands to fear God; explicit “soul” replaces an expected “you” to make the address universal.
rows.anchor: وهي معترضة بين جملة { اتقوا الله } وجملة { إن الله خبير بما تعملون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite soul in a command means every soul, as in the Quranic conditional “if any of the polytheists seeks your protection” and al-Hariri’s verse.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { نفس } يفيد العموم في سياق الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tomorrow” metaphorically names the future, bringing a distant time near because tomorrow is the next day; Arab usage and the verses of Qirad b. Ajdaʿ and Zuhayr illustrate it.
rows.anchor: وأطلق ( غد ) على الزمن المستقبل مجازا لتقريب الزمن المستقبل من البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “tomorrow” magnifies and makes the Day’s unknowable reality awe-inspiring.
rows.anchor: أي لغد لا يعرف كنهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “for tomorrow” states purpose: deeds are sent ahead for the sake and benefit of the Resurrection day.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لغد } لام العلة ، أي ما قدمته لأجل يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sending ahead” metaphorically describes present work done for future benefit, like preparing a home before travelers or sending a scout before an army; the opposite is leaving work undone.
rows.anchor: والتقديم : مستعار للعمل الذي يعمل لتحصيل فائدته في زمن آت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “fear God” reconnects the rationale after the intervening clause and intensifies the emphasis; conjunction makes the repeated command sound newly established.
rows.anchor: وإعادة { واتقوا الله } ليبنى عليه { إن الله خبير بما تعملون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God is fully aware of what you do” explains the call to piety, with inna functioning as a causal marker.
rows.anchor: فجملة { إن الله خبير بما تعملون } تعليل للحث على تقوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command to fear God can mean fear that motivates action; the second can mean persist in that piety, with God’s awareness measuring their effort.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { اتقوا الله } المذكور أولا مرادا به التقوى بمعنى الخوف من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning not to forget God addresses those who initially adopted Islam but later neglected piety, especially hypocrites, as in the description of hypocrites as transgressors.
rows.anchor: أي أهملوا التقوى بعد أن تقلدوها كما سيأتي أنهم المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming God explicitly instead of using a pronoun makes the sentence fully independent like a maxim and cultivates awe in the audience.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { إن الله خبير بما تعملون } إظهار اسم الجلالة في مقام الإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning pictures neglect of religion as a concrete condition leading to transgression; such turning away ranges from Jewish unbelief to the hypocrisy of some early Muslims.
rows.anchor: بعد أن أمر المؤمنين بتقوى الله وإعداد العدة للآخرة أعقبه بهذا النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known group who forgot God may be hypocrites: they lacked Islamic monotheism, so forgetting God describes ignorance of His unity and perfection; the author links this to the surah of Repentance.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يراد ب ( الذين نسوا الله ) المنافقين لأنهم كانوا مشركين

rows.speaker: رواية الترمذي
rows.claim: A Tirmidhi version says the Muhajir was a Bedouin, the Ansari belonged to ʿAbd Allah b. Ubayy’s group, and the Muhajir struck him with a stick; Ibn Ubayy then urged withholding support from the Prophet’s circle.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية للترمذي في هذا الحديث : ( أن المهاجري أعرابي وأن الأنصاري من أصحاب عبد الله بن أبي

rows.speaker: أهل السير
rows.claim: Biographical accounts identify the Muhajir as Juhjah of Ghifar, a hired worker of ʿUmar, and the Ansari as Sinan al-Juhani, an ally of Ibn Ubayy.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل السير أن المهاجري من غفار اسمه جهجاه أجير لعمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incident may be one event whose details varied in Zayd b. Arqam’s transmission, or two events in the same expedition.
rows.anchor: واضطرب الراوي عن زيد بن أرقم في صفتها ؛ ويجوز أن يكون قد حصل حادثتان في غزاة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “to God belongs the honor” creates an inverted restriction: honor belongs to God, His Messenger, and believers, not the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المسند على المسند إليه في { ولله العزة } لقصد القصر وهو قصر قلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the lām before the Messenger emphasizes his honor as grounded in God’s honor and promise; repeating it for believers stresses their dignity despite poverty and small numbers.
rows.anchor: وإعادة اللام في قوله : { ولرسوله } مع أن حرف العطف مغن عنها لتأكيد عزة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that hypocrites know parallels the earlier denial that they understand; repeating their name makes the sentence stand alone like a maxim.
rows.anchor: والقول في الاستدراك بقوله : { ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون } نظير القول آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lack knowledge because they ignore visible signs of Muslims’ growing power and their enemies’ decline since Badr.
rows.anchor: فلم يفطنوا للإقبال الذي في أحوال المسلمين وازدياد سلطانهم يوما فيوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns from exposing hypocrites to urging believers not to be distracted and to spend for good and communal needs, countering the order not to support the Prophet’s followers.
rows.anchor: إلى الإقبال على خطاب المؤمنين بنهيهم عما شأنه أن يشغل عن التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending must begin before death, when a person’s wish for more time to do good will be useless; the shift follows the hypocrites’ words, and wealth comes before children due to context.
rows.anchor: والمبادرة إلى ذلك قبل إتيان الموت الذي لا يدرى وقت حلوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing believers through the relative clause signals concern that they obey the prohibition.
rows.anchor: ونودي المخاطبون بطريق الموصول لما تؤذن به الصلة من التهمم لامتثال النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children are singled out because wealth absorbs time in acquisition and growth, and its accumulation can displace remembrance of the duty to give.
rows.anchor: ولأنها كما تشغل عن ذكر الله بصرف الوقت في كسبها ونمائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Care for children, managing their needs, and enjoying their company can also distract from remembering divine commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وأما ذكر الأولاد فهو إدماج لأن الاشتغال بالأولاد والشفقة عليهم وتدبير شؤونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording addresses wealth and children as the distractors but means their owners; the following “whoever does that” confirms this causal rhetorical construction.
rows.anchor: والمراد نهي أصحابها ، وهو استعمال معروف وقرينته هنا قوله : { ومن يفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second lā is a coordinating negative before “your children”; since prohibition implies negation, it reinforces the ban on being occupied by children as strongly as by wealth.
rows.anchor: و { لا } في قوله : { ولا أولادكم } نافية عاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr includes both spoken remembrance such as prayer and Quran recitation, and inward recollection through reflection on God and obedience; ʿUmar calls the latter superior at commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: فيشمل الذكر باللسان كالصلاة وتلاوة القرآن ، والتذكر بالعقل كالتدبر في صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Working for wealth and children is not blameworthy when it does not distract from God’s remembrance; such distraction has degrees.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن الاشتغال بالأموال والأولاد الذي لا يلهي عن ذكر الله ليس بمذموم

rows.speaker: علماء أصول الفقه
rows.claim: The warning that whoever does this is a loser supports the legal principle that a prohibition requires refraining from the act.
rows.anchor: دليل على قول علماء أصول الفقه ( النهي اقتضاء كف عن فعل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” means being distracted by wealth and children: abandoning required remembrance such as prayer on time and failing to observe divine commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والإشارة ب { ذلك } إلى اللهو عن ذكر الله بسبب الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distraction by anything other than wealth or children is even more deserving of the prohibition and warning.
rows.anchor: ومتى كان اللهو عن ذكر الله بالاشتغال بغير الأموال وغير الأولاد كان أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun rhetorically restricts “the losers” to those who disobey, exaggerating their loss; the demonstrative says they deserve that outcome.
rows.anchor: قصر صفة الخاسر على الذين يفعلون الذي نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spending command counters the hypocrites’ plot and applies both to the Prophet’s entourage and other recipients, so the sentence serves as a general conclusion.
rows.anchor: هذا إبطال ونقض لكيد المنافقين حين قالوا : { لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Spend” covers both obligatory and recommended giving because the imperative expresses an unqualified request shared by both.
rows.anchor: وفعل { أنفقوا } مستعمل في الطلب الشامل للواجب والمستحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From what We provided” frames giving as gratitude: the giver spends God’s favor in the way the divine law directs.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الإنفاق المأمور به شكر لله على ما رزق المنفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min means “some of”; this eases the command and includes fixed measures such as zakat, needs assigned by ability, cause-based expiations, and voluntary giving left to personal choice.
rows.anchor: وهذه توسعة من الله على عباده ، وهذا البعض منه هو معين المقدار مثل مقادير الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a hadith that charity extinguishes sins as water extinguishes fire.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث ( الصدقة تطفىء الخطايا كما يطفىء الماء النار )
